works: Signed intake (HMAC t.body, 5 min skew, constant-time) on POST /v1/calls, POST /v1/calls/{id}/end, GET /v1/calls/{id}; signed event batches to {VP_CONTROL_URL}/hooks/runtime with per-call seq, in-order delivery, same-batch retries, call.ended alone and last
No default stack: unknown or missing stack refused (422), missing credentials refused (503 with the names), voice and combinationId checked, never substituted

Per-contact facts reach the model as the contact rows block (after brief and memory, before the LAST block), in compile.ts contactRows() format; the door gets them as perContact facts. product/tests/agents-runtime.test.ts passes 4/4 against this runtime

Brief used verbatim; memory brief only when memoryStatus = loaded; generic data-driven LAST block per turn (spent facts and figures, stray caller figures, goals open/settled, cues, closing, crisis/opt-out/asked-AI state, marker rules)
Parity guard: vpvoice/rules.py refuses at import any rules.json key, builtin, scope or enum it does not implement, so an engine change breaks CI at load, not quietly in a call

Caller-crisis judge (judge.json): raise-only, default shadow, 800 ms bound, in parallel with the brain; raise interrupts the turn with the crisis path; off unless VP_LLM_SAFETY_JUDGE_* (or DEFAULT) is configured; raise in production only on the owner's go

Reply door = shared rules.json evaluated as index.ts does (all 1186 vectors pass) + runtime layer (first-breath clause, truth first, crisis lines); block -> one rewrite told the rule, then a safe line
Caller signals and redaction from rules.json; redacted text is what reaches transcript, events and the LLM
Transports: sim (text socket), webrtc (lab-style browser socket), sip (Plivo outbound dial + stream, Plivo/Exotel inbound streams, Plivo transfer for phone hand-off)
Cascade turn-taking ported from the lab (held replies, 1.4 s hold on unfinished speech, withdraw, barge-in by words, heard-text history); Gemini Live session with a door on its output transcription
Cost meter in integer milli-rupees at 95 INR/USD (ears/brain/voice/telephony; second/token/char), deltas that sum to the total; hard limits end the call; crisis stretches limits to 2x then hands off
Test calls: fallbacksUsed is always []; a failed component ends the call as error with the reason in GET /v1/calls/{id}
Dockerfile for Azure Container Apps (python:3.12-slim, non-root, healthcheck; copies the lab's Silero model and rules.json)
untested: The crisis judge against a real model (latency within 800 ms from India, verdict quality on blind sets): only fake models so far

Every real provider adapter (Gemini text/TTS/Live ears/Live s2s, Vertex route, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter text and speech, Azure Speech REST, Sarvam ears/brain/voice): ported from the lab, never run from this package; no keys were used from the coding sandbox
Azure voice over REST instead of the lab's pre-warmed SDK socket: first-audio latency not measured
Real browser client against /v1/media/browser (protocol documented in README; no page ships here)

Plivo dial, answer/hangup webhooks, stream, transfer and carrier hang-up against a live line; Exotel stream protocol (from docs only, no live line); Exotel outbound dialling is not implemented (refused 422)
Gemini Live session end to end (only its door cut is unit-tested); s2s in sim mode (GeminiLiveText) never run
Silero VAD in the turn-taking path (tests force the energy VAD; Silero load verified only)
Recording upload: recordingUri is a local file:// path when VP_RECORDINGS_DIR is set; no blob storage
Docker image build (no docker in the sandbox)
Latency and cut-in rates of the ported turn-taking on this runtime (lab figures do not carry over until measured)
contractGaps: call.ended has no field for the failure reason when endReason = error; it is logged and in GET /v1/calls/{id} only
The signature does not cover method or path; the runtime closes the replay hole on /end by requiring conversationId in the body
brief.hash is checked as sha256 hex of brief.text (optionally sha256:-prefixed); the control plane must hash the same way
Control-plane brief compiler should use the marker vocabulary in README (<end_call>, <goal:ID>, <tool:NAME>, <handoff:REASON>)
Judge shadow and unavailable outcomes are logged only, until calls adds the 'judge' RuntimeEvent to shared/runtime-protocol.ts; only judge_raised is a safety event (RD3 suspended_goal)
decisions: In a crisis, ticket limits stretch to 2x; at the ceiling the call is handed off (crisis_handoff); her <end_call> is ignored and a request for a human never ends the call unless a live transfer takes it
A recording refusal discards the whole recording, not just the rest of the call
Google route (Vertex or Gemini API key) is chosen once per call; 5xx retries stay on the same model and route
neverSay hits are reported under RD7, as the shared rules do
v2-live (Gemini Live) holds each turn until its transcript has passed the door: safe, but slower; recommend no production calls on it until its latency is measured with the hold
sharedRuleGapsFixed: The 9 gaps the runtime reported were fixed in rules.json at eaae1c1 (clause-scoped noneClause, local PIN context); they are normal tests now.

reviewFixes.B3: each sentence is doored alone and together with the previous sentence of the same reply
reviewFixes.B4: identity confirmed only by an explicit yes / "main hi" / the name, answering a question that named the person; greetings, questions back, silence and missing names never verify
